clusters.headline: US Air Force investigates suspected drone activity at RAF Lakenheath in England
clusters.summary: On November 13, U.S. Air Force security personnel responded to reports of unauthorized drone activity at RAF Lakenheath, a military base in Suffolk, England. The U.S. Air Force in Europe confirmed that no personnel, aircraft, or infrastructure were affected by the incident. British and American authorities are currently working together to investigate the origin of the drones. The situation has been resolved, and no injuries or damage were reported.

RAF Lakenheath is located in Suffolk, England
The 48th Fighter Wing operates out of the base

clusters.headline: London Metropolitan Police investigate comedian David Walliams for alleged sexual offenses
clusters.summary: The London Metropolitan Police have launched an investigation into British comedian and children's author David Walliams following allegations of non-recent serious sexual offenses. The probe follows reports from ITV News and The Guardian, which accused Walliams of grooming and sexually abusing girls and young women over a 20-year period. Walliams, 55, has denied all allegations and maintains he has not broken the law. Prior to the publication of these reports, Walliams unsuccessfully attempted to secure a court injunction to block the media outlets from releasing the story.
key_facts: Metropolitan Police Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney is overseeing the call for witnesses.
The ITV News and The Guardian documentary is titled 'David Walliams: Power and Silence'.
Walliams attempted to block the publication of the allegations by claiming it would lead him to commit suicide.
The allegations involve conduct spanning more than 20 years.
The Metropolitan Police statement was released on Friday, November 13, 2026.

clusters.headline: Probation officers in England and Wales vote for industrial action over pay and workloads
clusters.summary: Probation officers and family court staff represented by the Napo union have voted to take industrial action in response to a 5% pay offer and excessive workloads. Members have approved overtime restrictions beginning on 23 November, with plans to organize full strike action at a later date. The union claims the service is in crisis, exacerbated by the government's prisoner early release scheme. Napo officials warn that the service could face collapse if these issues are not addressed.
key_facts: Napo union members rejected a 5% pay offer.
Overtime restrictions are scheduled to begin on 23 November.
The union claims probation wages have stagnated since 2010.
Ian Lawrence is the general secretary of the Napo union.
Reception staff are reportedly paid just above the minimum wage.
clusters.outlet_disagreement: The Daily Mail frames the strike as a threat to public safety and a specific failure of the Labour government's early release scheme, whereas other outlets focus more neutrally on the union's grievances regarding pay and workload.

clusters.headline: Police investigate separate violent attacks in Romford and Watford
clusters.summary: Two separate violent incidents occurred in the United Kingdom involving arrests for attempted murder. In Romford, a 21-year-old man was arrested on November 13 after a Metropolitan Police officer was stabbed in the neck. Separately, in Watford, a 33-year-old man was arrested following an attack on 80-year-old Brenda Raymond, who was doused and set on fire in her apartment building on November 9. Ms. Raymond remains in critical condition with life-threatening injuries, while the police officer's injuries were determined to be non-life-threatening.
key_facts: Met Police officer stabbed in Romford at 4:16pm on November 13
Brenda Raymond, 80, attacked at Caractacus Cottage View in Watford
33-year-old suspect arrested for conspiracy to commit arson with intent to endanger life
Detective Inspector Adam Bridges described the Watford incident as an 'absolutely horrific attack'
Police believe a flammable liquid was used in the Watford assault
clusters.outlet_disagreement: The provided items cover two distinct criminal events, one involving a police officer in Romford and the other an elderly woman in Watford, which are unrelated.

clusters.headline: Reform UK faces scrutiny over security funding and recent electoral performance
clusters.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage is facing questions after reports revealed the party is paying for his personal security despite his previous claims that a £5 million gift from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne would cover these costs. Simultaneously, the party is navigating political challenges, including a decline in vote shares during recent local council by-elections and polling data suggesting the Conservatives have overtaken them in national support. Amid these struggles, Reform UK has launched a national security review, led by former RAF commander Angus MacIntyre, which labels Russia as Britain's greatest state threat.
key_facts: Reform UK is using central party funds to pay for Nigel Farage's security team and two cars.
Christopher Harborne stated his £5 million gift was intended to support Farage's security for life.
Reform UK saw its vote share fall in all five wards contested in recent local by-elections.
Angus MacIntyre, a former RAF commander, is leading Reform's new national security review.
The Conservatives have overtaken Reform UK in national opinion polls for the first time in two years.
clusters.outlet_disagreement: While British outlets focus on Reform UK's internal funding controversies and electoral struggles, the TASS report focuses on the unrelated rise of the AfD party in Germany.
